"You MAY banish an attack action card from your hand. IF YOU DO, IT gets +3{p} OR go again until end of turn." The payoff was a list under `additional_effects` on the BANISH node -- a key BANISH does not read -- so both halves were unreachable and the card only banished. It was also mandatory, and the banish target was the bare string "HAND" gated on an effect-level CARD_IN_ZONE, which asks whether SUCH A CARD IS SOMEWHERE IN HAND and then banishes whatever the target parser resolves; the restriction belongs on WHICH card, not on whether the effect runs.

"+3{p} OR go again" is a choice between two effects, which is what CHOOSE is for -- the previous authoring applied BOTH.

Approximation stated rather than hidden: "IT" is the banished card, and the buff is queued as "your next attack this turn" rather than pinned to that object. A banished attack action can only come back and be played by another effect, and the queue matches on card properties; the object-scoped pin added for sharp_incline_red is on the COST queue, not this one.
